name: Higher-risk building standards transition checker
demand: Search volume, installs, users, and paid demand are unverified. The best current population proxy is BSR’s July–September 2026 data: 114 new HRB/conversion Gateway 2 applications received and 186 in progress, covering 40,644 units in progress; separately, 466 HRB internal-work applications were received and 1,109 were in progress. These are regulated-work counts, not eligible customers: only some projects will need this specific transition check. The rules apply in England. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/building-safety-regulator-building-control-approval-application-data-july-to-september-2026/building-safety-regulator-building-control-approval-application-data-july-to-september-2026 https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026-letter
prices: The closest transition checker is free, with no sign-up or email wall, and asks whether work is HRB work; its page says different dates apply. Exact HRB result behavior is unverified. Part L Consultant lists developer work from £120 per plot, non-domestic work from £350, and a 2026 readiness review as quoted; these are services, not checker prices. MEPX shows no checker price. Adjacent product FireStrategy.ai offers free calculators and lists its broader engineering workspace at £299 per seat monthly or £249 monthly equivalent on annual billing. https://partlconsultant.co.uk/tools https://partlconsultant.co.uk/services https://www.mepx.co.uk/compliance-checker/ https://firestrategy.ai/pricing/
copy_speed: No dated launch announcement for an exact HRB/FHBS transition checker was verified. A close free Part L checker was live and maintained by 15 September 2026; its first launch date is unverified. MEPX’s broader compliance checker says its guidance was checked on 23 July 2026; its launch date is unverified. FireStrategy.ai had a Gateway 2 readiness checker reviewed 25 July 2026, an adjacent rather than exact substitute. Because the transition rules are published and the core check is date/status logic, copying the basic checker appears easy; actual copy time is unverified. https://partlconsultant.co.uk/guides/part-l-transitional-arrangements https://www.mepx.co.uk/compliance-checker/ https://firestrategy.ai/tools/gateway-2-readiness-checker/
platform_risk: Low platform dependence if this remains a standalone cited checker: the BSR has its own online application-management service, and no integration or partner is needed for a date/status result. API availability is unverified. Main risk is regulatory interpretation and updates: the HRB transition depends on a valid pre-deadline application not being rejected, staged protection can continue only while the original application is not rejected or lapsed, and the regulator/building control body retains decision authority. The Approved Documents were corrected in September 2026, showing that source maintenance is necessary. https://www.gov.uk/guidance/manage-a-building-control-application-for-a-higher-risk-building https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026-letter https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/building-regulations-circulars
defensible_asset: The statutory rules are public, and a date calculator alone has little defensibility. A plausible asset is a versioned UK rules engine with clause-level citations, tested edge cases, a change log, and a per-building decision record that tracks application validity and later stages. That could create modest workflow switching costs; customer retention and proprietary case data are unverified. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2026/335/enacted https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026-letter
build_effort: Unverified estimate. A basic checker is a narrow deterministic decision tree. A dependable paid product needs versioned rules, citations, regression cases for staged/rejected/lapsed applications and earlier transitional arrangements, plus a clear audit/export path. Agent automation can draft source-change diffs, reports, and support answers, but a qualified human should approve rule changes; the product does not need generative AI to make the core determination. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026-letter
channel: Brand-led SEO and a free cited checker, paid search, and opt-in professional-body or trade-newsletter placements fit a national software product without relying on Ricardo’s face. Keep electronic marketing consent-based and inbound: ICO guidance says electronic mail includes email, text, and social DMs, and unsolicited messages to individual subscribers, including sole traders, generally require consent or a valid soft opt-in; the ICO B2B guidance says it is under review following the Data Use and Access Act. https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/ https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/how-do-we-comply-with-the-pecr-electronic-mail-marketing-rules/
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; <=5 hours/week is a target, not an evidenced operating figure. It depends on self-serve onboarding, limited support, and human review of regulatory updates.
desk_test: Within one working day, compare the free Part L checker against the published rules using cases for a valid pre-deadline HRB application, a post-deadline application, a rejected or lapsed application, a staged application, and an earlier transitional arrangement. Record which outputs or cited milestones it does not provide. Make a one-page brand-only mock of that gap with a request for a paid pilot, then distribute through an opt-in professional channel or inbound search. Proceed only if a qualified team shows willingness to pay; do not use cold email, text, or DMs to individuals or sole traders. https://partlconsultant.co.uk/tools/part-l-transition-checker https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026/the-future-homes-and-buildings-standards-building-circular-012026-letter https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/
red_flags: The strongest concern is direct free competition: Part L Consultant already offers a free transition checker with an HRB selector and different-date messaging, so the proposed basic checker may already exist; its exact HRB outputs remain unverified. MEPX also offers a free-looking route checker. No independently verifiable payment or revenue evidence was found; published fees are asking prices, not proof of sales. The BSR project counts show activity but do not establish demand for a separate product. The trigger is narrow and time-bound, while high-stakes regulatory answers require careful sourcing and human review. The lead survives the legal-trigger check but does not yet pass commercial, differentiation, or <=5-hour/50%-automation validation. https://partlconsultant.co.uk/tools/part-l-transition-checker https://www.mepx.co.uk/compliance-checker/ https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/building-safety-regulator-building-control-approval-application-data-july-to-september-2026/building-safety-regulator-building-control-approval-application-data-july-to-september-2026
